subject: CCPA/CPRA: operator evidence and offshore transfer scenario
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@healthnexus.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthNexus Legal <legal@healthnexus.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 02:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — operator declaration + offshore subprocessors

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal at HealthNexus asked me to follow up with a narrow request: before we progress to procurement we need clear evidence that Redwood will act as a "service provider/operator" under CCPA/CPRA and not be treated as a "seller." Specifically they want: 1) a one-page attestation that Redwood processes HealthNexus personal data only to provide the service and does not perform targeted advertising or sell data, 2) a dataflow map listing subprocessors that will see telemetry (even if pseudonymized) including any offshore subprocessors, and 3) a contingency plan for onshore-only fallback if regulators or our DPO require it.

Two practical follow-ups for you: can you confirm whether any telemetry or aggregated logs are routed to any subprocessor outside the US (APAC/EU) for batching or analytics, and whether we can get an attestation signed (DocuSign) within two business days?

We appreciate this is a short timeline — our security team is trying to close the last open item in the privacy review.

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Grant
Senior Privacy Program Manager
HealthNexus

Subject: Re: Quick ask — operator declaration + offshore subprocessors

Oliver / Marissa —

Technical confirmation below:

1) Telemetry & Aggregation: Our default metrics/billing pipeline aggregates usage telemetry in an internal Kafka cluster and ships the aggregated batches to an analytics endpoint. Historically a small portion of our analytics processing (non-identifying aggregation jobs) ran in partner-managed clusters in EU/APAC for latency-cost reasons. For enterprise accounts requiring US-only processing we can pin the pipeline to run exclusively on our US cluster; that configuration is operational and we can enable it for HealthNexus before onboarding.

2) What counts as "telemetry": trade names in our roster: application-level usage counters, token counts, request timing, and error rates. We do not surface raw prompt/response content to third-party analytics vendors; raw content is retained only in our customer-tagged, encrypted S3 buckets and is not included in the analytics export.

3) KV cache & inference artifacts: KV cache used for model acceleration is ephemeral and stored on GPU-attached ephemeral disks; we do not persist it to third-party processors.

4) Fallback/Onshore path: enabling US-only analytics takes 24–72 hrs for a full cutover plus a short validation window (we can provide a checklist). If you require contractual language that guarantees US-only processing for telemetry we can add a clause to the DPA and provide the operational controls evidence (pipeline config snapshot, runbook).

I'll attach the SOC2 summary and a sanitized subprocessor list (we'll redact vendor contact info before external share).

-Ben
